$comment: The napkin script verb table. The text parser, the documentation generator, the CLI's verb listing and the helper skill read it; src/core/script/instructions.ts holds the matching types, and test/script-instructions.test.ts keeps the two in step field for field.

categories.title: Document
categories.summary: The page: its size, background and name, the unit bare numbers are read in, the seed, and more pages.

categories.title: Layers
categories.summary: Named layers and nested groups, with opacity, visibility and lock.

categories.title: Paint
categories.summary: What every mark after it is drawn with: tool, color, width, opacity, fill, gradient, outline, dash, profile, nib, font, and the hand-drawn pass.

categories.title: Shapes
categories.summary: Marks built from Bezier anchors: rectangles, circles, ellipses, lines, polygons, stars, arcs, spirals and the shape library, and marks combined as the Wipe Stacks and the Shape Stacker combine them.

categories.title: Paths
categories.summary: Marks written segment by segment, from SVG path data or from a block of steps, curves through points, and paths cut where a point lands on them.

categories.title: Transforms
categories.summary: Translate, rotate, scale and mirror, baked into the anchors of every mark after them, with push and pop to undo them.

categories.title: Control
categories.summary: Named numbers, reusable definitions, and repetition.

categories.title: Text and media
categories.summary: Text, placed images, linked files, and documents the host supplied.

categories.title: Effects
categories.summary: Blur, shadow and color effects for the next layer, group or mark, as CSS filter functions are: drawn in SVG, in PNG and in the app, and left out of a PDF.

categories.title: Output
categories.summary: Hints the renderers read: the box every output is cut to, and one box every page shares.

verbs.name: napkin
verbs.summary: The language version the script was written for. The first line of a script; without it version 1 is assumed, with a warning.

verbs.name: page
verbs.summary: The page size: a named size (a3, a4, a5, letter, legal, tabloid, square, slide, napkin) or a width and a height, turned portrait or landscape.

verbs.name: background
verbs.summary: The page color, or none for a transparent page.

verbs.name: name
verbs.summary: The page's name, and the file stem it is written under.

verbs.name: units
verbs.summary: The unit bare numbers are read in from here on: px, in, mm or pt. Pixels until changed.

verbs.name: seed
verbs.summary: The seed for the hand-drawn pass. One script and one seed draw the same bytes every run.

verbs.name: newpage
verbs.summary: Starts another page the same size, carrying the paint state across.

verbs.name: layer
verbs.summary: A drawing layer. Marks after it go on it until the next layer.

verbs.name: group
verbs.summary: A group layer. The layer and group lines in its block become its children.

verbs.name: clip
verbs.summary: A clip group: everything its block draws shows only inside the block's last closed shape, in paint order, which paints nothing while it clips - the app's Make Clipping Mask. Without a closed shape in it, the block is a plain group.

verbs.name: tool
verbs.summary: The kind of mark: pen (the app's Brush; brush is taken for it), marker (translucent, so overlapping passes build up like ink), copic (a broad, angled nib), pencil (a lead through the paper's grain; pencil picks one) or eraser (cuts its line's swath out of the marks drawn before it on its layer, as the app's Eraser does, and draws nothing of its own).

verbs.name: color
verbs.summary: The ink color of every mark after it.

verbs.name: width
verbs.summary: The stroke width of every mark after it.

verbs.name: opacity
verbs.summary: The opacity of every mark after it, from 0 to 1.

verbs.name: fill
verbs.summary: The fill color of closed shapes after it, or none.

verbs.name: gradient
verbs.summary: A gradient fill for closed shapes after it: linear at an angle, or radial from the centre out, or none.

verbs.name: stroke
verbs.summary: Turns the outline on or off. With it off, a closed shape is its fill alone.

verbs.name: style
verbs.summary: The outline's dash: solid, dashed or dotted.

verbs.name: profile
verbs.summary: How the width runs along a brush or marker stroke: uniform, rounded, tapered or wave.

verbs.name: nib
verbs.summary: The angle of the copic nib, in degrees.

verbs.name: pencil
verbs.summary: Takes up the Pencil at a grade: graphite alone, 9H to 9B, or charcoal (HB to 6B), compressed (2B to 6B) or vine (hard, medium, soft) and its grade. Every mark after it is drawn with that lead through the paper's grain, in its tone - or in the color given, a colored pencil. The width is the line's own; the app's softer leads draw broader at one tool width.

verbs.name: rough
verbs.summary: The hand-drawn pass for every mark after it: 0 is exact, 1 is clearly drawn by hand, and off is 0. Seeded, so it draws the same way every run.

verbs.name: font
verbs.summary: The font family and size of text after it.

verbs.name: rect
verbs.summary: A rectangle, with rounded corners when r is given.

verbs.name: circle
verbs.summary: A circle, drawn as four cubic curves rather than a polygon.

verbs.name: ellipse
verbs.summary: An ellipse, from its centre and two radii.

verbs.name: line
verbs.summary: A straight line between two points.

verbs.name: polygon
verbs.summary: A closed shape through a list of points, with rounded corners when r is given.

verbs.name: polyline
verbs.summary: An open line through a list of points.

verbs.name: star
verbs.summary: A star with the given number of points, between an outer and an inner radius.

verbs.name: arc
verbs.summary: An open arc of a circle between two angles, in degrees clockwise from three o'clock.

verbs.name: spiral
verbs.summary: A spiral winding out from its centre to the radius over the given number of turns.

verbs.name: shape
verbs.summary: A named shape from the built-in library, drawn in a box from x, y. With one size its longer side is that long and it keeps its proportions; with a width and a height it is stretched to fill them.

verbs.name: wipe
verbs.summary: Combines the marks its block draws, as the app's Wipe Stacks do, and draws what is left in their place: in (Wipe In, their union), out-front (Subtract Top from Below: the bottom one less the rest), out-back (Subtract Below from Top: the top one less the rest), mid (Mid Wipe: where all of them overlap), outer (Outer Wipes: where an odd number overlap) or clean (Clean Wipe: every piece of their overlaps, a mark each). What is left is painted as the topmost mark, or as the bottom one for out-front; text, pictures and eraser marks in the block are passed over. The block keeps its paint and transforms to itself, as a group does, and effects written just before it go on what it leaves.

verbs.name: stack
verbs.summary: Stacks the marks its block draws as the app's Shape Stacker does, at the pieces under its points - the places where the marks overlap and where they do not: merge makes those pieces one shape, painted as the topmost mark over the first point, and each mark keeps what was not merged; remove takes them away from every mark. Text, pictures and eraser marks in the block are passed over. The block keeps its paint and transforms to itself, as a group does, and the points are where the stack line is.

verbs.name: path
verbs.summary: One mark, from SVG path data or from a block of path steps. Each subpath of a compound path is one piece of the same mark.

verbs.name: move
verbs.summary: Starts a new subpath at a point.

verbs.name: to
verbs.summary: A straight segment to a point.

verbs.name: by
verbs.summary: A straight segment by an offset from the current point.

verbs.name: curve
verbs.summary: A cubic curve to a point, steered by two handles.

verbs.name: smooth
verbs.summary: A cubic curve whose first handle mirrors the last one, so the join stays smooth.

verbs.name: through
verbs.summary: A smooth curve through a list of points. Inside a path block it continues the subpath; outside one it is an open mark of its own.

verbs.name: close
verbs.summary: Closes the current subpath back to its start.

verbs.name: split
verbs.summary: Cuts the topmost mark drawn so far whose path passes within 4 px of a point, where the point lands on it, as the app's Split does: an open path becomes two, a closed one opens there, and a compound shape gives up the ring that was cut, as an open mark of its own. Nothing moves, and the pieces take the mark's place on its layer. In a wipe or a stack block it cuts among the marks the block has drawn.

verbs.name: smear
verbs.summary: A pass of the Smear, a blending stump, along a list of points: it spreads the graphite of every pencil mark drawn so far that it reaches, along the drag, as the app's Smear does. The width is the stump's, scaled by the transform as a width is, and the strength from 0 to 1. In a wipe or a stack block it smears among the marks the block has drawn.

verbs.name: warp
verbs.summary: Liquify's Warp, as the app's Liquify does it: a brush pushed from the point by dx and dy, carrying what is under its centre the whole way, like clay. The brush reaches the marks drawn so far whose outline passes within its radius of the point, under the transform as a mark drawn there would be, and its effect falls off smoothly to nothing at the rim; the radius scales with the transform. Pencil marks are the Smear's, and text, pictures and eraser marks have no outline to bend: all are left as they are. Each mark it bends is fitted again after, so its anchors stay few. In a wipe or a stack block it bends among the marks the block has drawn.

verbs.name: twirl
verbs.summary: Liquify's Twirl: turns what is under a brush at the point about its centre, by the angle in degrees there - clockwise on the screen, as rotate turns - and less toward the rim, so distances from the centre are kept. The brush reaches the marks drawn so far whose outline passes within its radius of the point, under the transform as a mark drawn there would be, and its effect falls off smoothly to nothing at the rim; the radius scales with the transform. Pencil marks are the Smear's, and text, pictures and eraser marks have no outline to bend: all are left as they are. Each mark it bends is fitted again after, so its anchors stay few. In a wipe or a stack block it bends among the marks the block has drawn.

verbs.name: pucker
verbs.summary: Liquify's Pucker: draws what is under a brush at the point in toward its centre, a point near the centre by the amount, 0 to 1, of its distance. The brush reaches the marks drawn so far whose outline passes within its radius of the point, under the transform as a mark drawn there would be, and its effect falls off smoothly to nothing at the rim; the radius scales with the transform. Pencil marks are the Smear's, and text, pictures and eraser marks have no outline to bend: all are left as they are. Each mark it bends is fitted again after, so its anchors stay few. In a wipe or a stack block it bends among the marks the block has drawn.

verbs.name: bloat
verbs.summary: Liquify's Bloat: pushes what is under a brush at the point out from its centre, a point near the centre by the amount, 0 to 1, of its distance. The brush reaches the marks drawn so far whose outline passes within its radius of the point, under the transform as a mark drawn there would be, and its effect falls off smoothly to nothing at the rim; the radius scales with the transform. Pencil marks are the Smear's, and text, pictures and eraser marks have no outline to bend: all are left as they are. Each mark it bends is fitted again after, so its anchors stay few. In a wipe or a stack block it bends among the marks the block has drawn.

verbs.name: push
verbs.summary: Saves the transform, the paint state and the units, for the next pop to restore.

verbs.name: pop
verbs.summary: Restores the transform, the paint state and the units the last push saved.

verbs.name: translate
verbs.summary: Moves everything drawn after it.

verbs.name: rotate
verbs.summary: Turns everything drawn after it, clockwise in degrees, about the origin or a point given with at.

verbs.name: scale
verbs.summary: Scales everything drawn after it, about the origin or a point given with at. One factor scales both ways.

verbs.name: mirror
verbs.summary: Reflects everything drawn after it: x swaps left and right across a vertical line, y swaps top and bottom across a horizontal one, at 0 unless given.

verbs.name: let
verbs.summary: Names a number for the expressions after it, in the current units.

verbs.name: define
verbs.summary: Records a block of drawing under a name without drawing it, for place to draw.

verbs.name: place
verbs.summary: Draws a definition, moved, scaled or turned.

verbs.name: repeat
verbs.summary: Runs a block a number of times, counting from 0 in the name given with as.

verbs.name: text
verbs.summary: A text item, measured and aligned, and editable in the app. With as marks the letters are drawn as brush strokes instead.
verbs.example: text "Acme Corp" at 200 70 size 28 align center

verbs.name: image
verbs.summary: Places an image: an asset the host supplied, by name, or a data URL. Nothing is read from disk.

verbs.name: link
verbs.summary: Places a linked file: one selectable element that references the file instead of drawing its contents into the page.

verbs.name: use
verbs.summary: Copies in a document the host supplied, as a group, with its layers and anchors.

verbs.name: effect
verbs.summary: An effect for the next layer, group or mark the script makes, as its CSS filter function works: blur, brightness, contrast, saturate, grayscale, sepia, invert, hue-rotate, opacity or drop-shadow. Several stack in order, and none clears what is waiting.

verbs.name: crop
verbs.summary: The box every output is cut to: auto fits the ink with room to spare, none keeps the page, or a box given outright.

verbs.name: registration
verbs.summary: One box every page is written in, so frames drawn by one script line up when they are played in sequence.

diagnostics.summary: A line starts with a word that is not a verb.

A verb where it cannot appear: a path step outside a path block, a napkin line after the first, a layer inside a path, a newpage inside a group or a definition, a layer, group, clip or use inside a wipe or a stack.
The verb, or this way of writing it, is known but not drawn by this build or by the host running the script; the instruction is skipped.
A number, or an expression in parentheses, was expected.
A length was expected: a number, a number with a unit (10mm, 0.5in, 12pt, 4px), a percentage, or an expression.
A double-quoted string was expected.
A bare name was expected: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
A CSS color was expected, such as #1f2328, red or rgb(31, 35, 40).
One word from a fixed list was expected; the message lists them.
A list of points was expected: x y pairs separated by commas.
A list of gradient stops was expected: (color offset, color offset, ...).
Something is left on the line after the instruction was read, or a character that cannot start anything.
A required argument is missing; the message names it and shows how the verb is written.
A block was expected: { at the end of the line, the instructions it holds, and } to close it.
A block opened with { is never closed with }.
A } closes a block that was never opened.
A string runs to the end of the line without its closing quote.
An expression could not be read: an unknown operator, a missing operand, or an unclosed parenthesis.
A number carries a unit the language does not know. The units are px, in, mm and pt, and % for a share of the page.
A value is out of range: an opacity above 1, a negative radius, a star with fewer than 2 points, a percentage where the page cannot measure one.
The script does not start with napkin <version>; version 1 is assumed.
The script names a version newer than this build reads; the message names the newest it does.
An expression uses a name no let or repeat has set.
place names something no define recorded.
shape names something the shape library does not have.
image names an asset the host did not supply.
use names a document the host did not supply.
An image's size cannot be read from its data, so it is placed square: 100 by 100, or the one size given by itself.
text as marks has a character the built-in face does not draw; it is left as a gap.
An instruction in a JSON script has a field its verb does not have; it is left out.
A definition places itself, directly or through another definition.
An expression divides by zero.
The script ran more instructions, drew more marks, emitted more anchors or sampled points, or nested deeper than the limit allows; what it drew up to that point is kept.
pop with nothing saved to restore.
A push is never popped before its block ends; the saved state is restored there anyway.
A second define replaces an earlier one of the same name.
A linked file could not be read for an output that has to draw it, so its placeholder was drawn instead.
An effect nothing took: no layer, group or mark followed it before its block, its page or the script ended.
A wipe's or a stack's block drew marks it cannot combine - text, pictures, linked files, eraser marks - and they are drawn as they are.
A wipe or a stack left nothing: out-front's bottom mark wholly covered by the rest, say, or a stack remove taking every piece.
A wipe or a stack could not combine its block's marks - fewer than two it can combine, more than it takes, or geometry it could not make - so they are drawn as they are.
A stack point is on none of the pieces its block's marks make, so it picks nothing; the message says which.
A split point is within 4 px of no path drawn so far, or lands on the end of an open one, so nothing is cut.
A clip block drew no closed shape to clip with, so it is a plain group.
A smear reaches no pencil mark drawn so far, so it spreads nothing.
A warp, twirl, pucker or bloat reaches no mark it bends drawn so far, so it bends nothing.
An eraser line reaches text or a picture, which it cannot cut, and passes over it.
